name: Wälzlager-Zentrum Süd GmbH
summary: Wälzlager-Zentrum Süd is a family-owned bearing distributor founded in 1975, with 120 staff and EUR 46.8 M turnover. It is financially stable (credit index 181, unchanged; equity 34 %) and is narrowing its focus to large key accounts. It now calls our 0.5 % share 'not strategic' and wants standard items supplied from stock at list conditions, with individual agreements not extended. Our framework expires 2026-12-31. The supplier has opened the renewal by asking for our volumes, but its RFQ quote for 6306 is 5.5 % above its own list quote.

situation.decision_maker: Owner decides on prices and has offered to open the calculation. The new sales director is the gatekeeper and treats us as a small account.

negotiation_pattern: Annual renewal asks ranged from 1.6 % to 7.1 % (mean asked 4.13 %). Settlements averaged 1.78 %, and four of nine renewals settled at 0 %. It used to give back about 2.35 pts per round. Since mid-2026 it has hardened to a list-price policy: no discounts on standard items, and only multi-year volume agreements change prices. For the 6306 renewal it quoted 4.63 vs its own list quote of 4.39 (+5.5 %).
wants: multi-year volume agreement (contract_months up, committed volume_per_year)
volume concentration / higher share (we hold 70 % / 40 % / 100 % quotas)
reliable volume forecasts (asked for expected volumes)
punctual payment on the agreed 30 days (we pay late 85 % of the time)
low-effort standard business: list/stock items, few individual deals
protects: unit_price on standard items (list conditions policy)
individual/special agreements (will not extend for small accounts)
stock-only supply model (no dedicated stock or special lead-time commitments)

trades.give: contract_months up to 24-36 with an annual volume_per_year commitment and forecasts across all three bearings
trades.get: unit_price on 360020 held at 4.39 (no +5.5 %) and 360021/360022 at current prices, fixed per year
trades.why: They said only multi-year volume agreements change prices. This turns their own rule into our lever.

trades.give: volume_per_year up: raise quota on 360021 from 40 % and 360020 from 70 %
trades.get: continuation of an individual framework agreement (not plain list terms) and a price freeze
trades.why: It wants customers with volume, so bundling makes us look bigger. Our spend has grown from 180k to 217k.

trades.give: payment_days: commit to strict on-time payment at 30 days net
trades.get: lead_time_days 7 confirmed contractually plus stock availability commitment on 360022
trades.why: This is a cheap goodwill fix: we currently pay 3.1 days late on average. Skonto has little value to them because they are not cash-short.

trades.give: accept an open-book review of the calculation offered by the owner
trades.get: any increase capped at a justified cost delta (well below 5.5 %)
trades.why: The owner volunteered transparency, and that is the route to fact-based, smaller settlements.

arguments.point: Your RFQ quote of 4.63 for 6306 is above your own list-condition quote of 4.39 from two weeks earlier. We expect at least list.
Our spend with you has grown every year (180,530 → 192,796 → 216,969 EUR). We can offer a multi-year, bundled volume agreement, which is exactly what you said moves prices.
Under clause 3.1, price changes need written notice at least 60 days before year end (by 1 Nov 2026). Prices remain fixed otherwise.
We would take up the owner's offer to walk through hourly rates and material, so any change is cost-based.
OTD has stayed at 83-87 % against the 95 % target in the quality agreement. A price increase without a delivery improvement is hard to justify internally.

avoid: Threatening to move volume or terminate. At 0.5 % of their turnover they may simply let us go, and 360022 has no second source.
Demanding a cut below list on standard items. This directly hits their stated policy.
Offering skonto or early payment as the main currency. They are not cash-short.
Hard pressure tactics with the new sales director. Address the owner respectfully instead.
Continuing late payments during the negotiation.
tone: Write in a respectful, factual, partnership tone addressed to the owner. Lead with volume growth and a multi-year offer, then raise the list-price inconsistency calmly.
red_flags: They may not renew: they said individual agreements will not be extended. The framework can be terminated with 60 days' notice, i.e. by 1 Nov 2026.
Single source on 360022 (7309 BEP, 100 % quota, no other source), now offered 'from stock only'. Qualify a second source.
We are deprioritised: called 'not strategic' and replies are slower. This means allocation risk in a shortage.
OTD is persistently 83-87 % against the 95 % target; ppm is about 300 with 9 complaints recharged at EUR 150 each.

evidence.claim: Family-owned, financially stable: credit index 181, unchanged over 12 months; equity ratio 34 %.
Refocusing on key accounts; smaller customers served from standard ranges at list conditions; individual agreements not extended.
Our volumes called 'not strategic'; replies slower since summer.
Only multi-year volume agreements change prices on standard items.
Renewal quote for 360020 is 4.63 vs current and list price of 4.39 (+5.5 %).
History: mean asked 4.13 %, settled 1.78 %; several renewals settled at 0 %.
Framework expires 2026-12-31 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 60 days' notice; prices are fixed per calendar year with a 60-day change notice.
360022 is single-sourced and offered at list from stock only.
OTD of 85.0 % and ppm of 302 fall short of the 95 % OTD target.

indicators.credit_index: 181 (12 months ago 181; higher is worse, >300 weak)
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 86.7, ppm 387) → 2026Q1 green (otd 83.1, ppm 345) → 2026Q2 green (otd 86.8, ppm 283) → 2026Q3 green (otd 85.0, ppm 302)
